plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and build cash.

conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target monthly return around 1.5%. It significantly reduces leverage and concentration, holding a larger cash buffer. Expect lower drawdowns but also capped upside potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL to 3% and 2% respectively.
Trim SPY to 23% to slightly reduce concentration.
Add QQQI to 10% for income diversification.
Buy PANW as a new, high-scoring long setup.
Add to CRWD to increase exposure to a strong performer.
This plan balances growth with risk reduction.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets around 2.5% monthly growth with a risk-first approach. It trims leverage and concentration while adding quality names and income. Expect moderate drawdowns and a blend of growth and stability.

plan: Increase leveraged ETFs SOXL, MUU, METU, and SPAL.
Buy PANW and NBIS as new, high-scoring long setups.
Add to CRWD to increase exposure to a strong performer.
This plan concentrates on high-conviction names and leverage.
Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% monthly growth by leaning into leverage and concentration on top-rated setups. It accepts significantly higher potential drawdowns and the risks of leveraged ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is paramount.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU) and high-beta names (CRWD, SNOW).
Trim SPY to 20% to increase cash and reduce concentration.
Significantly increase QQQI to 40% for maximum income focus.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions over growth.
Expect very low drawdowns and reliable, though variable, income.
NAV can still decline in market selloffs.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% monthly distributions by focusing on income-generating ETFs like QQQI. It minimizes leverage and high-beta single names, prioritizing capital preservation and steady cash flow. Distributions are not guaranteed and NAV can fall.
